answer: One apiary backs one identity. The keeper registers hive count, GPS site and a health certificate with the agriculture office, renewing each season and filing a yield log per harvest; unannounced inspections; a hive idle on the horizon of the season loses its weight. Each fake costs one real apiary: 800 units for hives and bees, 150 for the opal-sealed certificate, 120 days of tending — 100 fakes cost 95,000 units. Rented hives fail the seal check, bought honey fails a pollen test, and a falcon-eyed audit matches flight logs to bloom, so copied yields expose the cluster and revoke it.
